The configuration of the planar perovskite solar cells with PCBM/PEG network is illustrated in Figure 1a. The fabrication of organic-network PSC is similar to that of planar heterojunction PSCs. The perovskite precursor solution is prepared by PbCl2 and CH3NH3I (MAI) at a 1:3 molar ratio in N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF). PCBM is dissolved in chlorobenzene, and added into the perovskite precursor solution followed by PEG (See methods for more details). The PCBM/PEG/perovskite blending solution is spin-coated on FTO/TiO2 substrate, followed by the thermal annealing at around 100°C to form the perovskite film with PCBM/PEG network.

Device/Film 1~4 will be labelled as no PCBM/PEG, +PCBM, +PCBM/PEG, +PEG in the figures, respectively.

To get the perovskite solution, CH3NH3I and PbCl2 were dissolved in anhydrous N,NDimethylformamide(DMF) at a 3:1 molar ratio with final concentrations of ~35 wt%. As PCBM has very low solubility in DMF, it was firstly dissolved in chlorobenzene at a concentration of 50 mg ml -1 . For PCBM-perovskite film, PCBM/chlorobenzene solution (90  l ml -1 , 5.4‰ mole ratio to perovskite) was added into the perovskite solution. For PCBM/PEG network perovskite film, PEG (molecular weight: 20,000; 20 mg ml -1 , 1.1‰ mole ratio to perovskite) was firstly added into the perovskite solution under stirring at 60°C for 12 h. Then PCBM/chlorobenzene solution was added in perovskite solution.

Here a device structure is developed with organic network uniformly incorporated into the organic/inorganic hybrid perovskite film by one-step solution-processing strategy, which significantly improves the photovoltaic performance and long-term stability of planar type perovskite solar cells. unresolved_notes: The source reports PbCl2 and CH3NH3I precursor ratios but does not explicitly report one final bulk perovskite formula; no absorber formula was inferred.
The source does not explicitly identify the polarity as n-i-p or p-i-n, so polarity remains not_reported despite the ordered stack.

Device 1-4 are design labels used across J-V, MPP tracking, impedance, population, and ambient-stability experiments. The evidence does not establish that the same physical cell was reused across those protocols; separate J-V, MPP, and impedance devices were therefore retained.

Forward and reverse J-V observations include the reported outcomes only. Shared protocol conditions were AM1.5 irradiation at 100 mW cm -2 in a glove box, scan velocity 200 mV s -1, forward range -0.1 V to 1.5 V, and reverse range 1.5 V to -0.1 V.

The low-, optimized-, and higher-PCBM-content arms (1.8‰, 5.4‰, and 10.0‰) are concentration/process variants rather than separate device families. The source reports qualitative group outcomes but does not provide atomic individual-device J-V values for the 1.8‰ and 10.0‰ arms; no individual devices or performance observations were invented for them.

The 5.4‰ PCBM content is explicitly reported for the fabricated PCBM-containing films and is represented in the Device 2 and Device 3 absorber families. The 1.8‰ and 10.0‰ optimization arms are not represented as separate families.

The detailed PEG concentration, mole ratio, stirring temperature, and stirring duration in the methods are explicitly scoped to the PCBM/PEG-network recipe. They were not propagated to the PEG-only Device 4 recipe. Only the explicitly shared PEG-containing spin speed was applied to Device 4.

The source reports the ambient-aging decay from 14.5% to 3% ~ 4% within 50 ~ 100 hours collectively for 'devices without PEG', encompassing Device 1 and Device 2. It does not give separate outcomes for those two families, so this comparison remains one unlinked stability specimen rather than two falsely separated tests.

The population evidence gives 'More than 100 devices' across Device 1-3 and a figure caption says '~100 samples'; it does not provide an exact per-family sample size, so sample_size is null for each population record.
The reported table labels PCE values without displaying a percent sign in each row. Raw table values were preserved as printed rather than silently adding percent signs.
Film-only SEM, optical, PL, XRD, EDS/HRTEM, NMR-solution, and micro-grid specimens were excluded because they are not complete photovoltaic devices.

The source does not establish that forward and reverse scans were performed on the same physical cell. The repaired J-V observations therefore use separate scan-specific device records rather than preserving the unsupported shared dev-jv-1 through dev-jv-4 identities.

The low (1.8‰), high (10.0‰), and optimized (5.4‰) PCBM passages discuss Device 2 and Device 3 optimization together, but do not identify which complete PCBM-only or PCBM/PEG stack each reported outcome belongs to. No additional device families were created from these concentration arms.

The PEG stock concentration, PEG-to-perovskite ratio, stirring temperature, and stirring duration are explicitly stated for the PCBM/PEG-network perovskite recipe. Their application to the PEG-only Device 4 recipe is not explicit, so these values were not propagated to Device 4.

The statement 'More than 100 devices' concerns the combined Device 1-3 fabrication and measurement set and does not establish a per-family sample size. It was not newly propagated as a separate count for each family.

The MPP and impedance passages identify Device 1-4 or Device 1-3 by design label but do not unambiguously establish whether each label denotes one physical specimen. Existing dev-mpp-* and dev-is-* records were therefore not removed or relinked solely from the unclaimed-record flags.
